2. The plaintiffs-respondents-petitioners instituted a suit for permanent injunction and the short fact of the case is that the suit land has originally belonged to Aminuddin Pramanik and Shaharon Mai Bibi and the CS Khatian was duly recorded in their name. While Amiruddin and Shaharon Mia were in peaceful possession of the suit land by purchase they wanted to sell the land for necessity of money, then Shibran Mohanto, the predecessor of the plaintiff purchased the suit land on 14-11-1942 by a registered deed and became the owner and possessor of the suit land. Subsequently SA Khatian was duly prepared in the name of Shibran Mohanto who died leaving behind his two sons namely, Mohabir and Shukdeb. Thereafter on the death of Shukdeb the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 became his heirs and after the death of Mohabir the plaintiff No. 3 became his heir. They have been possessing the suit land on payment of rent and in some portion of Plot No. 613/1080 they constructed homestead and in Plot No. 614 they planted fruit trees such as mango, jack-fruit, lichi trees, etc. They have been enjoying the property for 55/56 years. On the other hand, the defendants have got no right, title and possession in the suit land. On 12-7-1997 AD the defendants threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs forcibly from the suit land and thereafter on 25-7-1997 they tried to erect some huts in some portion of the suit land but due to strong resistance of the plaintiff they could not erect any hut. The defendant is threatening the plaintiff continuously to dispossess him from the suit land hence the plaintiff was constrained to institute the suit. 

 3. On the other hand, the defendants-opposite parties contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and stating, inter alia, that Shahar Mai Bibi was the tenant under the original landlord Najargpat Singh and others. Subsequently, Shahar Mai Bibi sold the suit land to Amiruddin Paramanik, the predecessor of the defendants in CS record. That out of 3.28 decimals of land 2.02 decimal was in khas possession of Amiruddin and he made pattani settlement of the remaining land and it was recorded in CS Khatian Nos. 87, 88, 91, 92 and 93 respectively. That Shibran Mohanto, predecessor of the plaintiff, was a borgadar under Amiruddin Paramanik and thereafter SA khatian was wrongly prepared in the name of Amiruddin Paramanik and Shibran Mohanto which Amiruddin did not know in his life time. Since Shibran Mohanto did not give the borga crops regularly, so Amiruddin Paramanik returned back the land in his own possession. Thereafter, when settlement operation for preparing SA record was started the fake right of Shibran Mohanto was cancelled. 

 8. Mr Alauddin Ahmed, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondents-petitioners, submits that the plaintiff has been able to prove the case successfully by producing the original title deed dated 24-11-1942 and the certified copy of the CS Khatian, SA Khatian, rent receipts and other connected papers which were proved and exhibited as Exhibit-1, 2, 3, 4 and rent receipts as Exhibits series 5. 

 9. The plaintiff examined as many as 4 witnesses to prove the possession of the suit land. The plaintiff Ganesh Mohanto was examined as PW 1 who categorically stated in his evidence that the entire case of the plaint was proved and exhibited the original registered deed of the year 1942 as Exhibit 1 and CS Khatian Exhibit 2, SA Khatian Exhibit 3, BCR Exhibit 4 and rent receipts Exhibits 5 series. The PW 2 Abdus Sobhan, PW 3 Sharifuddin and PW 4 Mominuddin were examined to prove and corroborate the PW 1 with regard to the possession of the plaintiff in the suit property. Next, he submits that the learned Additional District Judge, Rangpur did not at all apply his judicial mind in assessment of the evidence of the PWs, particularly the evidence of PW 1 plaintiff and also did not consider the original registered title deed over 55 years old, CS Khatian, SA Khatian, DS Khatian and rent receipts. The observation made by the lower appellate Court that in the CS Khatian the name of Shahar Mai Bibi should not be published along with the name of Amiruddin, because she transferred her share to her husband Amiruddin before publication of CS Khatian. The learned Counsel further submits that this finding of the learned Additional District Judge, Rangpur is manifestly perverse, because it is neither the case of the plaintiff nor the case of the defendant and he has made out a third case of transfer without any basis and no such transferred deed or document was produced before the Court by any parties. Finally, the learned Counsel submits that the cardinal principle of law followed in reversing the finding of the trial Court, the lower appellate Court should reverse the finding with reference to the evidence on record assigning the cogent ground. But the lower appellate Court without applying his judicial mind and without considering the evidence on record and Exhibits i.e. 55 years old original registered title deed, original CS, DS, RS Khatian and series of rent receipts, disbelieved the case of the plaintiff without assigning any cogent reason occasioning failure of justice which is liable to be interfered by this Court. In support of his contention the learned Counsel referred the decision in the case of Shishir Kanti Pal and others vs Noor Muhammad and others reported in 55 DLR (AD) 39 wherein it is stated: 

 12. On a meticulous examination of the evidence on record, documents, khatian, rent receipts and judgment of both the Courts below and other connected paper, it transpires that the trial Court discussed the evidence and also perused the documents, exhibits and also considered the material evidence on record and made his clear observation in decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiff. The lower appellate Court without applying his judicial mind gave much importance in determining the title of the suit land without considering the prime factor of possession. In the instant case, the plaintiff examined 4 witnesses to prove his title in the suit land and also to prove his possession and all the 4 witnesses categorically stated in their evidence that the plaintiff has been living in the suit land since the purchase of the suit land in the year 1942 i.e. about 55 years. On the other hand, the defendant claimed that they purchased the same suit land in the year 1997 and since then they have been in possession of the suit land but the defendant could not prove any act of possession by adducing cogent evidence. Moreover, it appears from the title deed of the plaintiff that Amiruddin Promanik and his wife Shahar Mai Bibi purchased the suit land by a registered deed on 24-11-1942 and the original document was produced and exhibited by the plaintiff and three other PWs stated in their evidence that the plaintiff has been living in the suit land since long, as such, the plaintiff is in consistent possession of the suit land since purchase. Therefore, the plaintiff has been able to prove his title and possession over the suit land by producing original title deed and by adducing oral evidence proved his possession in the suit land.
